steps.say: Renovascular hypertension is driven by renal artery narrowing. The Goldblatt model is demonstrated by experimental clipping. Renin-angiotensin release is triggered by the starved kidney. Systemic pressure is held high by salt retention. Flash pulmonary oedema is recognised as a clue. Small asymmetric kidneys are measured carefully on imaging.
steps.tx: **Renovascular hypertension** (artery driven high pressure) follows the **Goldblatt model** (clip kidney experiment): clamping one renal artery fires **renin-angiotensin** (salt rescue hormones) release from the starved kidney, holding pressure high. Think of it with flash pulmonary oedema or a small asymmetric kidney, because revascularisation can cure.

vis.alt: Kidney diagram showing prerenal hypoperfusion with reduced blood flow.
vis.caption: Prerenal hypoperfusion: a starved kidney fires renin-angiotensin. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Atherosclerotic stenosis is found commonly in older smokers. The ostium and proximal third are affected most typically. Over 90 percent of renovascular cases are atherosclerotic. Diffuse vascular disease is present widely elsewhere. Resistant hypertension is investigated routinely with duplex scanning. Ostial stenting is selected carefully for suitable lesions.
steps.tx: **Atherosclerotic stenosis** (furring of the artery) crusts the **ostium** (mouth) and **proximal third** (first segment) in older smokers with diffuse disease, causing over **90%** (nine in ten) of renovascular cases. Hunt it with resistant hypertension and a abdominal bruit, because stenting selected ostial lesions helps.

steps.say: Fibromuscular dysplasia is recognised early in young hypertensive women. Mid and distal arteries are affected typically with beading. String-of-beads appearance is seen clearly on angiography. About 10 percent of renovascular cases are dysplastic. Flank bruits are heard commonly in many patients. Angioplasty is curative in most suitable cases.
steps.tx: **Fibromuscular dysplasia** (beaded artery disease, **FMD** (non inflammatory wall disease)) draws the classic **string-of-beads** (bead necklace) of alternating stenoses and aneurysmal bulges in mid and distal arteries of young women, causing about **10%** (one in ten) of cases. Suspect it with early severe hypertension and a flank bruit, because angioplasty cures most.

steps.say: Medial fibroplasia is identified clearly as the commonest subtype. Eighty five percent of FMD lesions are medial. Fibromuscular ridges are alternated regularly with thin media. Perimedial and intimal forms are recognised as rarer. Media stress is blamed reasonably for the distribution. Histology is confirmed only after surgical specimens.
steps.tx: Medial fibroplasia leads the **FMD subtypes** (dysplasia flavours) at **85%** (eighty five), with rings of fibromuscular ridges alternating with thin media, while **medial fibroplasia** (middle coat scarring) names the histology itself. Perimedial and intimal forms trail behind, because media bears the stress.

steps.say: PTRA is performed routinely for uncomplicated fibromuscular disease. Angioplasty without stenting is completed carefully using balloons alone. Cure over 80 percent is reported widely in series. Bending arteries are spared permanent metal scaffolds. Dissection or recoil is stented promptly as a bailout. Restenosis is reduced markedly by avoiding routine metal.
steps.tx: Uncomplicated FMD takes **PTRA** (balloon only widening), **angioplasty without stenting** (no metal left), because balloons alone cure over **80%** (eight in ten) and stents invite restenosis in bending arteries. Reserve stents for dissection or recoil, because metal fixes complications, not routine curves.

steps.say: Stenting in atherosclerosis is reserved strictly for selected lesions. Ostial recoil is countered reliably by metal scaffolds. Severe bilateral disease is treated readily by stenting. Solitary kidneys are protected routinely with metal scaffolds. Medical therapy is optimised carefully alongside intervention. Statins and pressure control are continued lifelong afterwards.
steps.tx: Ostial atherosclerotic plaques recoil after balloons, so **stenting in atherosclerosis** (metal scaffold) pins the mouth open and holds pressure gains where trials allow. Select severe bilateral or solitary kidney disease, because routine stenting adds little. Optimise medicines first, since stents never replace statins and control.

steps.say: Renal artery aneurysm is monitored closely by size criteria. Repair over 2 cm is advised strongly electively. Childbearing age is treated surgically at any size. Pregnancy rupture is feared most of all complications. Coiling or stenting is performed electively before emergency. Kidneys are saved reliably by planned elective repair.
steps.tx: **Renal artery aneurysm** (kidney artery bulge, **RAA** (bean artery balloon)) threatens rupture most in pregnancy, so repair is advised over **2 cm** (two centimetres) or at any size in **childbearing age** (fertile years). Coil or stent the sac electively, because emergency rupture repair kills kidneys.

vis.alt: Arterial diagram and CTA showing saccular aneurysm morphology.
vis.caption: Saccular aneurysm shown in another vessel: renal aneurysms are repaired over 2 cm. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Arteriovenous malformations are recognised clinically as congenital tangled nests. Cirsoid AVM is confirmed clearly on angiography. Haematuria with flank bruit is reported as the classical pair. Transcatheter embolization is performed electively for complete closure. Acquired fistulae are watched carefully initially after biopsy. Many post-biopsy leaks are closed spontaneously without intervention.
steps.tx: Congenital **arteriovenous malformations** (tangled short circuits), the **cirsoid AVM** (tufted nest), bleed with haematuria and a **flank bruit** (whooshing sound), closed by **transcatheter embolization** (glue through a tube). Acquired **arteriovenous fistulae** (single hole shunts), classically **post-biopsy AVF** (needle track leak), often shut alone under watch.
